.NET MAUI 10.0.130

.NET MAUI 10.0.130 Release Notes

.NET MAUI 10.0.130 introduces significant improvements across all platforms with focus on quality, performance, and developer experience. This release includes 123 commits with various improvements, bug fixes, and enhancements.

Ai Agents

  • Add probability-scored duplicate issue detection by @kubaflo in #39218

Blazor

  • [inflight/current] Fix BlazorWebView root component subscriptions on disconnect (#39247) by @kubaflo in #39252

    🔧 Fixes
    • [Android] BlazorWebViewHandler never unsubscribes from RootComponents.CollectionChanged on disconnect, retaining the old MauiContext and finished Activity

  • Fix iOS BlazorWebView callbacks after disconnection by @sheiksyedm in #39430

    🔧 Fixes
    • BlazorWebViewHandler.iOS.cs NullReferenceException when web view has been disconnected

  • [WPF] Fix BlazorWebView disposal hanging when cleanup awaits JS interop by @sheiksyedm in #39497

    🔧 Fixes
    • [WPF] BlazorWebView.DisposeAsync never completes when a scoped service or component awaits JS interop on disposal

    • [Android] CollectionView GridItemsLayout: span lookups over uncached positions are O(position) per cell, O(position²) when grouped — ScrollTo last group takes ~38 s for 10 000 items, scrolling up after a jump stutters

entry.title: aws/aws-sdk-net - Releases - 2026-11-09
entry.content:
4.0.366.0

4.0.366.0 (2026-11-09 19:43 UTC)

  • Batch (4.0.105.0)
    • Adds support for additional Amazon EKS security context settings in AWS Batch. Pod-level settings include fsGroup, runAsUser, runAsGroup, runAsNonRoot, and seccompProfile. Container-level settings add Linux capabilities and seccompProfile to existing runAsUser, runAsGroup, and runAsNonRoot support.
  • BedrockAgentCore (4.0.117.0)
    • Adds the InvokeWebSearch API, which searches the web using the AWS-managed web search and returns ranked results with a text extract from each page. Results can be filtered by domain and by publication time.
  • DataZone (4.0.113.0)
    • Adds support for Workday Data Connect and Workday Live Data Query connection types in Amazon DataZone connection APIs.
  • ECS (4.0.111.0)
    • Amazon ECS Managed Instances now supports isolated and confidential tasks, which run in AWS Nitro Sandboxes. Configure them with trustedExecutionConfiguration in task definitions and nitroEnclavesEnabled in capacity providers.
  • Elasticsearch (4.0.102.0)
    • Adds cloned blue-green upgrades for Amazon OpenSearch Service domains. UpgradeElasticsearchDomain accepts DeploymentStrategyOptions to upgrade on a cloned cluster, the new UpdateClone API shifts search traffic, cuts over and sets retention, and DescribeDomainChangeProgress reports upgrade details.
  • Evs (4.0.103.0)

Bugs Fixed

  • Fixed CodeTransparencyClient permanently rejecting the service TLS connection after a ledger CCF node certificate is reissued (for example, after a node pod restart). Maps v5.0.0 - Our Final Maps Release

CommunityToolkit.Maui.Maps v5.0.0 - Our Final Maps Release

The good news is that you no longer need us! In .NET 10, MAUI added Windows support to .NET MAUI's own Map control, meaning CommunityToolkit.Maui.Maps is no longer needed.

We recommend moving to .NET MAUI's official Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Maps package.

What changes in this release

  • UseMauiCommunityToolkitMaps, its AppBuilderExtensions class and the Windows handler MapHandlerWindows are marked [Obsolete].
  • The CommunityToolkit.Maui.Maps code will be removed from our repo when we merge our .NET 11 PR (#3331)

How to migrate

  1. Remove the CommunityToolkit.Maui.Maps package, its using CommunityToolkit.Maui.Maps; directives and the UseMauiCommunityToolkitMaps() call.
  2. Add the Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Maps package. The toolkit package used to reference it for you.
  3. Call builder.UseMauiMaps() in MauiProgram.cs on every platform.
  4. On Windows, also add an Azure Maps key: builder.ConfigureEssentials(essentials => essentials.UseMapServiceToken("YOUR_AZURE_MAPS_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY")). Without a valid key the Windows map shows no map data. See Manage authentication in Azure Maps to get one.

What to expect on Windows
.NET MAUI's Windows map is the WinUI 3 MapControl backed by Azure Maps.

  • Supported: MoveToRegion, the Street, Satellite and Hybrid map types, traffic, scrolling, zooming and pins.
  • Not supported yet: IsShowingUser, polygons, polylines and circles in MapElements, pin labels and info windows, and MapClicked.

Learn more

  • .NET MAUI Map documentation
  • Deprecation discussion: CommunityToolkit/Maui#3190
  • CommunityToolkit.Maui Map documentation

What's Changed

  • Add Device Tests, Apply Fixes for Bugs Found by @TheCodeTraveler in #3344

MediaElement v11.0.0 Bug Fix-A-Palooza

MediaElement v11.0.0 Bug Fix-A-Palooza 🎉

We have FINALLY implemented Device Tests! These are platform-specific unit tests that run on iOS, Android, MacCatalyst and Windows. This allows us to unit test all platform-specific code and has MASSIVELY increased our Unit Test Code Coverage to 91.8% Code Coverage on CommunityToolkti.Maui.MediaElement.

Breaking Changes

To fix certain bugs, and re-align features to ensure they behave the same across all platforms, we did have to modify some APIs and the associated underlying behavior. Please find the features you use, below, and update your apps accordingly.

All packages
  • API: Null arguments throw ArgumentNullException at the call. Public and protected members of the five libraries now guard the non-nullable reference parameters they cannot handle (about 275 guards).
    • A null that used to cause a NullReferenceException later (or was stored silently) fails at the call, with a ParamName. What to do: fix the caller.
    • An async member throws from the call itself, before it returns a Task.
    • Null arguments that a member handled before are still accepted, for example an IProgress<double> or a Paint background of null.
    • Feature-specific effects are listed in each feature's section.
    • BasePlatformBehavior guards only bindable. A null platform view passes through, because the Android IconTintColorBehavior accepts it.
  • Setup: CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core on Android adds a <queries> entry for the launcher (MAIN/HOME) to the app's merged manifest through the package's library manifest (src/CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core/AndroidManifest.xml). Badge needs it on Android 11 and later. If your app or Play listing reviews <queries>, check the merged manifest.
  • Setup: Dependencies: on Windows, CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core references System.Speech 10.0.11 (it was 10.0.1). No action is needed unless you pin the package. This comes from #3288 on main, not from this PR.

New APIs In This Release

  • Popup now declares IPaddingElement, which it already inherited from ContentView
  • GravatarImageSource declares IStreamImageSource, which it already inherited from StreamImageSource, and overrides Cancel() (see GravatarImageSource, after that ApiCompat run);
  • [SupportedOSPlatform("android23.0")] on the Android StatusBarBehavior (see StatusBar and StatusBarBehavior).
  • DefaultPopupSettings.BackgroundColorDark and OnInitializing (#3345)
  • NumericValidationBehavior.Interval (#3329)
MediaElement
API
  • Null arguments: FileMediaSourceConverter.ConvertFrom(null) throws ArgumentNullException.
  • Null arguments: MediaFailedEventArgs rejects null for its non-nullable members.
Behavior
  • An exception thrown by an event handler while Source changes is reported through MediaFailed.
    • Before, an exception from a StateChanged, PropertyChanged or PropertyChanging handler reached the code that set Source, or ended the app when MAUI set it from XAML or a binding.
    • Now it is logged and the change goes on. The first exception is reported once through MediaFailed: ErrorMessage names its type and message, and CurrentState is not set to Failed.
    • What to do: handle MediaFailed, and check ErrorMessage before treating every MediaFailed as a failed source.
  • MediaElement playback.
    • SeekTo clamps a position outside the media to its start or end and raises SeekCompleted. On iOS such a seek never completed.
    • SeekTo fails with the platform's exception, for example InvalidOperationException before the player is ready, where that exception ended the app.
    • Play() at the end of the media starts it again on iOS and Mac Catalyst, as on Android.
    • On Android, CurrentState reports Buffering while buffering (it was Paused) and Stopped at the end of the media.
    • A source without data empties the player and reports None.
    • What to do: check code that relied on the old states.
  • A disconnected handler stops the position timer. The MediaElement no longer keeps its page alive after the page is left. No action is needed.
    • Why: the dispatcher timer stops when the handler disconnects, and starts again when a handler connects later.
    • Found on iOS: a probe left the Sample's MediaElementPage alive 3 of 3 times after it was left (0 of 3 with the fix). The same leak is fixed and tested on Android, Mac Catalyst and Windows.
    • On Windows, MediaOpened arrives on the player's worker thread. An open that was still running when the handler disconnected no longer starts the timer again: the timer starts on the UI thread, and only while a handler is attached.
    • A second leak was in the Sample: MediaElementFromStreamPage was IAsyncDisposable, so the window's service scope kept every page that was opened.
      • iOS: a probe left the page alive 3 of 3 times before the change, 0 of 3 after.
      • Windows (the Sample at 4a8d407, 5 visits, a GC dump after the 5th Back): 0 MediaElementFromStreamPage, MediaElement or StreamMediaSource stay alive, GC heap 6.5 MB. With the Sample change reverted: 5 of each, 167.7 MB.
  • Also fixed: FileMediaSourceConverter.ConvertFrom had an inverted condition. A real path threw InvalidOperationException, and an empty or white-space string returned a source. Now a real path returns the FileMediaSource, and an empty or white-space string throws InvalidOperationException, as documented.

What's Changed

  • Add Device Tests, Apply Fixes for Bugs Found by @TheCodeTraveler in #3344
  • Apply MediaElement.Speed when playback starts on iOS and fix inverted AreFloatingPointNumbersEqual by @ne0rrmatrix in #3327
  • Fix iOS MediaElement support for multiple ItemsViews and windows by @ne0rrmatrix in #3222
  • Fix ios media element start bug by @ne0rrmatrix in #3281

  • CameraView.ErrorOccurred and ErrorOccurredEventArgs (#3299)

Breaking Changes

CameraView
API
  • Null arguments: ErrorOccurredEventArgs, MediaCaptureFailedEventArgs and CameraInfo reject null for their non-nullable members.
Behavior
  • Failures are reported through events instead of exceptions.
    • StartCameraPreview(CancellationToken) no longer throws for a camera that cannot start (except in the Android failed-connection case below). It raises ErrorOccurred on every platform.
      • A cancelled token still throws OperationCanceledException.
      • A view without a handler still throws InvalidOperationException.
    • The commands let no exception escape:
      • CaptureImageCommand, StartVideoRecordingCommand and StopVideoRecordingCommand report through MediaCaptureFailed.
      • StartCameraPreviewCommand and StopCameraPreviewCommand report through ErrorOccurred.
    • Failures of the handler's own work (connecting, switching to SelectedCamera, applying ImageCaptureResolution) raise ErrorOccurred instead of ending the app.
    • Android:
      • A preview without the camera permission now fails, is reported, and stays stopped until the activity resumes with the permission. iOS and Mac Catalyst report a denied permission the same way.
      • CaptureImage before the camera has started throws CameraException instead of waiting until its token is cancelled.
    • What to do: subscribe to ErrorOccurred and MediaCaptureFailed instead of relying on try/catch.
  • Android: one ErrorOccurred for a failed connection. A StartCameraPreview called while the CameraView connects to its camera waits for the connection.
    • When the connection fails and raises ErrorOccurred, that StartCameraPreview throws the same failure to its caller instead of raising ErrorOccurred again. StartCameraPreviewCommand doesn't report it again.
    • What to do: catch the exception where you await such a start.
  • StopCameraPreview cancels starts that still wait. StopCameraPreview and StopCameraPreviewCommand now cancel a pending StartCameraPreview, a pending StartVideoRecording (both overloads), the start the view makes when it connects its camera, and a camera switch.
    • The cancelled start throws OperationCanceledException, with no ErrorOccurred or MediaCaptureFailed. A start that a stop interrupted needs a new start.
    • What to do: do not treat that exception as a failure.
    • On iOS and Mac Catalyst, StartCameraPreview with an already-cancelled token throws and no longer starts the session.
  • Video recording.
    • Android: a StartVideoRecording during a recording replaces it: the new stream receives the video, and the earlier recording's video is discarded. Camera 6.1.0 ignored the second start; iOS and Mac Catalyst already replaced it.
    • Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows: a start that arrives while an earlier start still waits for the platform joins it. It returns once that recording has started, its stream receives no video, and it throws the earlier start's failure. On iOS and Mac Catalyst this holds for a double tap too, where Camera 6.1.0 replaced the first recording.
    • StartVideoRecording returns only once the platform has started the recording (#3311), so await it before relying on the recording. On iOS and Mac Catalyst, a start cancelled while it waits releases the recording state.
    • Windows, as on Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst:
      • StopVideoRecording waits for a pending StartVideoRecording.
      • A StartVideoRecording or a second StopVideoRecording that arrives while a stop waits for Media Foundation to finish the recording waits for that stop.
    • StopVideoRecording throws CameraException on Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst when the platform reports a recording with no playable video. A recording the platform ended early that has usable video is still returned.
    • Android: when the photo session cannot be restored after a successful export, StopVideoRecording still returns the video, and the failure is raised through ErrorOccurred. Selecting another camera during a recording waits until the recording stops or is replaced.
    • Windows: a StopVideoRecording whose token is cancelled already or while the stop finishes the video:
      • It still stops the recording and throws OperationCanceledException, as on Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst. It used to ignore the token and return the video.
      • The next StopVideoRecording returns the video. A StartVideoRecording that comes first discards it and puts its stream back, as for a replaced recording.
      • The camera that the recording turned on is off again when the cancelled stop throws.
      • A cancelled stop while a start or another stop is still pending throws without stopping anything.
      • With no recording, a cancelled StopVideoRecording returns Stream.Null on every platform.
      • StopVideoRecordingCommand ends without an event.
      • Camera 6.1.0 already handled a cancelled stop this way on Android and iOS; Mac Catalyst follows iOS.
      • Catch the OperationCanceledException and call StopVideoRecording again to get the video.
    • Windows: a StartVideoRecording during a recording ends and finishes the running recording and discards its video.
      • The running recording's stream goes back to the length and position it had when that recording started.
      • The video goes to the stream of the latest start, as on Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst. The camera stays on in between.
      • Camera 6.1.0 prepared a second recording without ending the first, so the first video was left unfinished or the new stream stayed empty.
      • If you relied on the first recording continuing, call StopVideoRecording before a new start.
    • What to do: handle ErrorOccurred and CameraException. On Android, don't rely on a second start being ignored.
  • Recording while the preview is stopped starts the camera.
    • On Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows, StartVideoRecording after StopCameraPreview, or before StartCameraPreview, starts the camera and then the recording. Android already did; Camera 6.1.0 recorded nothing on iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows.
    • A camera that the recording turned on turns off again when the recording ends. After a cancelled StopVideoRecording on Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst, it turns off only once the next stop returns the video.
    • A preview that the app started stays on.
    • When the camera can't start, a stopped preview stays stopped. On iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows, StartVideoRecording throws the failure: for example a CameraException without a camera or without the camera permission, or on Windows an UnauthorizedAccessException when the privacy settings block the camera. StartVideoRecordingCommand reports it through MediaCaptureFailed.
    • On Android, a StartCameraPreview after SetExtensionMode on a stopped preview shows the SelectedCamera. Camera 6.1.0 kept showing the camera that was selected when SetExtensionMode ran.
  • Windows: a start while the preview runs, and a stop during a recording.
    • StartCameraPreview while the preview already runs is a no-op.
    • A StartCameraPreview while an earlier start is still opening the camera releases that start's MediaCapture, so the camera is never held twice.
    • StopCameraPreview during a recording ends the recording, like on Android. A later StopVideoRecording returns Stream.Null, so do not expect a video from a recording that a stop ended.
Smaller changes
  • CameraView with an app's CameraViewHandler.PlatformViewFactory:
    • The camera shows in the factory's view, which the toolkit doesn't dispose.
    • On Windows, only a MediaPlayerElement shows the preview. Another element shows none, and a warning is written to the trace output.
  • CameraView on Android applies ZoomFactor and IsTorchOn again after another screen, such as FileSaver's save dialog or Home.

What's Changed

  • CameraView: Fixed crash on Windows when app has no camera access anymore by @MFinkBK in #3299
  • Add Device Tests, Apply Fixes for Bugs Found by @TheCodeTraveler in #3344

v16.0.0 Bug Fix-A-Palooza

v16.0.0 Bug Fix-A-Palooza 🎉

  • 96.7% Code Coverage on CommunityToolkit.Maui.Camera

  • 91.8% Code Coverage on CommunityToolkti.Maui.MediaElement

And thanks to the new Device Tests (along with excellent contributions from the community), this Release contains fixes for a whopping 58 Issues. 💪

Breaking Changes

To fix certain bugs, and re-align features to ensure they behave the same across all platforms, we did have to modify some APIs and the associated underlying behavior. Please find the features you use, below, and update your apps accordingly.

All packages
  • API: Null arguments throw ArgumentNullException at the call. Public and protected members of the five libraries now guard the non-nullable reference parameters they cannot handle (about 275 guards).
    • A null that used to cause a NullReferenceException later (or was stored silently) fails at the call, with a ParamName. What to do: fix the caller.
    • An async member throws from the call itself, before it returns a Task.
    • Null arguments that a member handled before are still accepted, for example an IProgress<double> or a Paint background of null.
    • Feature-specific effects are listed in each feature's section.
    • BasePlatformBehavior guards only bindable. A null platform view passes through, because the Android IconTintColorBehavior accepts it.
  • Setup: CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core on Android adds a <queries> entry for the launcher (MAIN/HOME) to the app's merged manifest through the package's library manifest (src/CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core/AndroidManifest.xml). Badge needs it on Android 11 and later. If your app or Play listing reviews <queries>, check the merged manifest.
  • Setup: Dependencies: on Windows, CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core references System.Speech 10.0.11 (it was 10.0.1). No action is needed unless you pin the package. This comes from #3288 on main, not from this PR.

New APIs In This Release

  • Popup now declares IPaddingElement, which it already inherited from ContentView
  • GravatarImageSource declares IStreamImageSource, which it already inherited from StreamImageSource, and overrides Cancel() (see GravatarImageSource, after that ApiCompat run);
  • [SupportedOSPlatform("android23.0")] on the Android StatusBarBehavior (see StatusBar and StatusBarBehavior).
  • DefaultPopupSettings.BackgroundColorDark and OnInitializing (#3345)
  • NumericValidationBehavior.Interval (#3329)
AvatarView
Behavior
  • AvatarView.
    • HorizontalOptions, VerticalOptions, HeightRequest, WidthRequest, Padding, Stroke, StrokeThickness and StrokeShape are no longer local values, so an implicit AvatarView Style applies (and a Border Style with ApplyToDerivedTypes).
    • An empty image source shows Text on every platform; iOS, MacCatalyst and Windows had previously showed an empty circle. Set Text to string.Empty or "" to display a blank circle.
    • The text replaces a failed or empty image only once the image has been laid out (about one layout pass later), because a GravatarImageSource asks for its picture only after its image has a size. So:
      • An AvatarView whose Gravatar failed to load while the page opened offline shows the picture again when the Email changes or a new load succeeds.
      • Such an AvatarView may show an empty circle for that one layout pass before the text.
Badge
Setup
  • CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core adds a <queries> entry for the launcher (MAIN/HOME) to Android apps; Badge needs it on Android 11 and later (see All packages).
Behavior
  • Badge on Windows without package identity. In an unpackaged app, Badge.SetCount writes one trace line and returns, instead of throwing a COMException that ended the app. No badge appears, so package the app if you need the taskbar badge.
Camera
  • See Camera v7.0.0: https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/Maui/releases#release-7.0.0-camera
ColorAnimationExtensions
Behavior
  • BackgroundColorTo and TextColorTo with a rate of 0 throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException from the call. Before, the error came later on the animation ticker and ended the app. Pass a rate above 0.
DialogFragment (Android)
Behavior
  • Android modal pages and the status bar. DialogFragmentService lays the dialog of a modal page out like the activity's window, for every status bar color.
    • On Android 11 and newer, a modal page receives the status bar inset. It must keep clear of the status bar itself, as a page in the activity's window does.
    • On Android 10 and older, a modal page also receives window insets with a transparent status bar color, where it received none.
DrawingView
Behavior
  • DrawingView.
    • On iOS and Mac Catalyst, GetImageStream with no lines returns Stream.Null instead of throwing InvalidOperationException, and a NaN image size, or one that is infinite on both sides, throws ArgumentException. Handle Stream.Null where you caught the exception.
    • An image scaled to ImageOptions.DesiredSize has its pixel size rounded half away from zero on Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst, as Windows already did. A 1920 x 1080 target of a 411 DIP canvas gives 1920 x 934 on Android, where it gave 1919 x 934.
    • On Windows a line captures the pointer, so a line released outside the view completes with DrawingLineCompleted, a lost capture raises DrawingLineCancelled, and a second pointer no longer starts or changes a line. No action is needed unless you worked around the old behavior.
Smaller changes
  • An unloaded view keeps its handler and listens again when it is loaded. DrawAction draws in a canvas state of its own.
Expander
Setup
  • Windows, iOS and Mac Catalyst: UseMauiCommunityToolkit registers the Expander layout handler (see Behavior below), so keep calling it at startup. That handler keeps its own platform view even when the app sets LayoutHandler.PlatformViewFactory.
Behavior
  • Expander accessibility.
    • On Windows the Expander is a Tab stop that Enter and Space toggle. UI Automation exposes it as a Button with the ExpandCollapse and Invoke patterns.
    • On Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst the header is one element for TalkBack and VoiceOver, with expand and collapse actions.
    • The Expander's internal layout now resolves to an internal ExpanderLayoutHandler, so a handler an app registers for Grid no longer applies to the Expander's internal Grid; LayoutHandler.Mapper changes still apply.
    • On Windows, iOS and Mac Catalyst, an app's LayoutHandler.PlatformViewFactory no longer creates the platform view of that layout, so the layout keeps the platform view that gives the header this support. The factory still creates the platform views of the app's other layouts, including the ones in the Expander's Header and Content, and on Android also the platform view of that layout.
Smaller changes
  • Expander Direction can be changed again by bindings and Styles.
FileSaver and FolderPicker
API
  • Null arguments throw ArgumentNullException at the call; FileSaver and FolderPicker still return the exception in the result. (see All packages)
Behavior
  • FileSaver and FolderPicker.
    • progress reports percentages from 0 to 100. It reported fractions from 0 to 1 during the copy, then a final 100, so remove any * 100 you applied.
    • A stream that cannot seek no longer fails the save; it gets only the final report.
    • On Android, a document whose provider gives no file path, such as a cloud document, is a successful save whose FilePath is its content:// URI. It used to fail with FileSaveException. Open such a path with the ContentResolver.
    • A null fileName or stream (and a null initialPath for FolderPicker) comes back as an ArgumentNullException in the result, without showing the picker.
GravatarImageSource
Behavior
  • GravatarImageSource.
    • The email is trimmed and lower-cased before hashing, as Gravatar requires, so mixed-case addresses now load their real image.
    • The download is fully read into a seekable stream, so on Windows the picture shows again. HttpClient.Timeout limits the whole download, and a body that fails halfway gives Stream.Null.
    • One load no longer cancels another.
    • A load that you start with CancellationToken.None never throws. Only a token that you pass and cancel makes GetStreamAsync and the default Stream function throw OperationCanceledException, instead of returning Stream.Null. .NET MAUI catches it for the loads that it cancels itself, so a view keeps the picture of the load that replaced it.
    • Cancel() ends only the loads started without a cancelable token, which then return Stream.Null. Its task always completes with true.
    • What to do: catch the exception where you call Stream or GetStreamAsync with your own token.
  • GravatarImageSource in a Button.
    • The picture is requested at the smaller of the WidthRequest and HeightRequest that the Button sets, or at Gravatar's default 80 pixels, and again when those requests change. It was requested at the Button's laid-out size, so on iOS and Mac Catalyst each picture made the Button larger until it was as wide as the screen (older than this PR).
    • Image, ImageButton and AvatarView still request the size they are laid out at.
    • A Button without size requests now gets an 80-pixel picture instead of one the size of the laid-out Button: on a 420 dpi Android screen, a 30 dp icon instead of 15 dp. Set HeightRequest on the Button for a smaller picture.
    • Windows: the picture is drawn whole, at most at its natural size, and scaled down to the room the Button has for it. The Button no longer grows for it.
      • Before this change, the picture loaded on Windows only with this PR's download fix (see the GravatarImageSource change above). It was then stretched to the Button's width, and the Button clipped it to a thin band.
      • A Button whose image is above or below its text (ContentLayout Top or Bottom) needs a HeightRequest that leaves room for the picture.
      • A Button without Text needs a HeightRequest or MinimumHeightRequest. The .NET MAUI app template's Button style sets MinimumHeightRequest to 44.
      • This works around a .NET MAUI behavior: on Windows, MAUI limits a Button's picture to its natural size only when it sees the BitmapImage's ImageOpened event, which a picture decoded from a stream has already raised.
KeyboardExtensions
Smaller changes
  • KeyboardExtensions on iOS and Windows call the platform on the UI thread. IsSoftKeyboardShowing called from another thread blocks until the UI thread answers. The tasks of HideKeyboardAsync and ShowKeyboardAsync complete once the UI thread has done the work.
Maps - See Maps v5.0.0: https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/Maui/releases#release-5.0.0-maps
MaxLengthReachedBehavior
API
  • Null arguments: MaxLengthReachedEventArgs rejects null for its non-nullable members.
Behavior
  • Keyboard dismissal. MaxLengthReachedBehavior hides the keyboard only while its own InputView has the focus, and through the view's own window. So Android no longer hides the keyboard of the view the user moved to, and the keyboard goes away in a modal page or a Popup too. No action is needed.
MediaElement
  • See MediaElement v11.0.0: https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/Maui/releases#release-11.0.0-mediaelement
NavigationBar (Android)
Behavior
  • NavigationBar (Android). The default Color is still transparent, but it is now a plain default value, so reading the color no longer makes IsSet true. As a result:
    • A page that never set a color no longer gets one applied.
    • Clearing Color or Style gives the window back its original color.
    • From Android 15 the color is drawn as a view over the navigation bar.
    • What to do: check pages that relied on the old default.
Popup
API
  • Null arguments: Options.SetPopupDefaults(null) and SetPopupOptionsDefaults(null) no longer store null.
  • Null arguments: The async void PopupExtensions.ShowPopup overloads throw to the caller instead of posting the exception to the SynchronizationContext.
Behavior
  • BackgroundColor is null by default, and Styles now apply. Margin, Padding, HorizontalOptions, VerticalOptions, CanBeDismissedByTappingOutsideOfPopup and BackgroundColor are now default values. 15.0.1 set them as local values in the constructor.
    • A Style can set them, and Popup.BackgroundColor reads null until something sets it.
    • A popup without a background shows DefaultPopupSettings.BackgroundColor, or in the dark theme BackgroundColorDark: black with #3345 in this release, where 15.0.1 showed white.
    • What to do: set BackgroundColor where a fixed color is needed, and check popups in the dark theme.
  • Navigation that removes a popup page ends ShowPopupAsync. When navigation removes the popup page without CloseAsync, ShowPopupAsync completes and Closed is raised exactly once. Before, neither happened, and code that awaited it stayed suspended.
    • Such navigation: Shell switching to another Shell element, PopModalAsync or PopAsync called by other code, Window.Page being replaced, or Shell popping the popup out of a modal NavigationPage.
    • Both happen one dispatcher cycle after .NET MAUI has removed the popup page, so a Closed handler can show another popup.
    • The result is the existing "closed without a result" shape:
      • WasDismissedByTappingOutsideOfPopup is true. It now means "closed without a result: by tapping outside the popup, or because navigation removed it"; it is false only after CloseAsync.
      • For ShowPopupAsync<TResult>, Result is null for a reference or nullable type. Reading it for a value type such as int throws PopupResultException, as after a tap outside.
    • What to do: check WasDismissedByTappingOutsideOfPopup first. Subscribe to Closed if you must tell a tap from a navigation removal.
    • If navigation removes the page before .NET MAUI reports that it was navigated to, Closed is raised without a preceding Opened.
    • A CancellationToken used as a timeout keeps working.
    • With a Shell as the root page, CloseAsync and ClosePopupAsync of a popup shown on a modal NavigationPage close only the popup. CloseAsync used to pop the whole page and never complete, and ClosePopupAsync threw PopupBlockedException.
    • A close that finds another page on top when it runs throws PopupBlockedException and pops nothing:
      • CloseAsync, Popup.CloseAsync and ClosePopupAsync (also through IPopupService) wait for earlier popup operations. When the close finally runs, they check again that the popup is still the page on top.
      • This applies when another page was pushed above the popup in the meantime, for example a popup that ShowPopupAsync was showing, or a modal page your code pushed. They already threw PopupBlockedException and popped nothing when that page was on top at the call.
      • Before, including in 15.0.1, they popped that other page and then never completed, so no popup in the app could open or close again. In some layouts they reported the popup closed while it stayed on screen.
      • ClosePopupAsync still targets the popup that was the most recent when you called it, not the newer one. Call it again to close the newer one.
      • A tap outside the popup or the Android Back button does nothing in this case. It no longer crashes the app if that other page is already on top when the tap runs.
    • A tap outside the popup, or the Android Back button:
      • no longer crashes the app (through async void) when an earlier tap, Back or navigation has already closed the popup;
      • ignores a pop that .NET MAUI canceled, where it crashed the app (on iOS and Mac Catalyst a NavigationPage cancels a PopAsync that waited behind a navigation that failed). The popup stays open, and a later tap closes it.
  • ShowPopupAsync, CloseAsync and ClosePopupAsync throw OperationCanceledException when the app cancels the navigation.
    • When the app cancels the navigation that removes a popup (a Window.ModalPopping or Application.ModalPopping handler that sets e.Cancel, or a Shell.Navigating handler that cancels), Popup.CloseAsync, Popup<T>.CloseAsync, ClosePopupAsync and IPopupService.ClosePopupAsync throw OperationCanceledException. The popup stays open and usable, Closed is not raised, and the navigation lock is released.
    • When a Shell.Navigating handler cancels the navigation that shows a popup (ShowPopupAsync of a Shell, or of a page or INavigation under a Shell root), every ShowPopupAsync overload, also through IPopupService, throws OperationCanceledException and nothing is shown.
    • Before, these calls never completed. A close that the app canceled also held the navigation lock, so no popup in the app could open or close again, and the tap outside the popup stopped working.
    • ShowPopup and the tap outside or Android Back show nothing, or do nothing, and throw nothing.
    • To tell this from your own token, catch OperationCanceledException when (!token.IsCancellationRequested).
    • A .NET MAUI limitation that this PR does not change: in a Shell whose current tab has a page pushed below the popup, a ModalPopping handler that cancels makes .NET MAUI retry the pop in a loop, so CloseAsync cannot return. Cancel in Shell.Navigating there instead.
Smaller changes
  • A popup shown from OnDisappearing of a modal page that is closing appears on the page below.
  • A WidthRequest or HeightRequest larger than the window is limited to the window.
  • Opened is raised once per show.
  • PopupClosed and Closed are raised after the navigation lock is released, in the same order as before.
RatingView
Smaller changes
  • RatingView redraws when FillOption changes.
SelectAllTextBehavior
API
  • Null arguments: SelectAllTextBehavior on Windows throws ArgumentNullException instead of InvalidOperationException for a null platform view (only a derived class can reach it).
SemanticOrderView
Behavior
  • SemanticOrderView on Windows sets the Tab order. Check the Tab order of screens that use it.
    • The views of ViewOrder that the container holds are listed first in its tab focus children, followed by the rest of its content.
    • A TabIndex that the app set is no longer overwritten. The exception: views of ViewOrder that a control within the container (a ScrollView, for example) holds, or that are outside the container, still get a TabIndex from the order.
    • It does not change Narrator's scan order, which follows the visual tree.
Smaller changes
  • An app's ContentViewHandler.PlatformViewFactory no longer creates the SemanticOrderView's platform view, so ViewOrder applies.
    • The factory still creates the platform views of the other content views and pages.
    • To customize that view, override CreatePlatformView in a handler derived from SemanticOrderViewHandler, and register it after UseMauiCommunityToolkit.
Snackbar and Toast
Behavior
  • Windows Toast and Snackbar remove only their own notification. Each removes its notification by Id. No action is needed unless the app relied on the old clear-all (below).
    • Before, a Toast.Show or Toast.Dismiss after an earlier toast, and a Snackbar.Show or Snackbar.Dismiss while a snackbar was shown, removed every notification of the app (AppNotificationManager.RemoveAllAsync). That included the other alert and the notifications the app shows itself, on screen and in the Action Center.
    • Since a Show no longer clears the app's other notifications, a Toast or Snackbar shown while another notification banner of the app is on screen waits behind that banner, as Windows queues banners.
    • Show now returns once Windows lists the new notification. That takes up to 1 s longer when Windows lists nothing for the app, for example while its notifications are off. A Snackbar whose Duration is zero or less does not wait.
    • Overlapping Show and Dismiss calls now take effect in call order. A call whose token is cancelled before its turn removes nothing and throws OperationCanceledException.
    • Do not block on a Show or Dismiss Task inside a Shown or Dismissed handler: .Wait() and .Result deadlock there.
Smaller changes
  • Snackbar on Windows:
    • It is dismissed at the end of Duration, raises Dismissed once and runs its action on the UI thread.
    • Show can take up to 1 s longer while the app's notifications are off (see Behavior above).
    • Show no longer throws for a Duration such as TimeSpan.MaxValue or TimeSpan.MinValue.
  • Snackbar on Android: a Duration below 1 ms shows it for 1 ms, and Dismissed is raised once.
  • Toast on Windows is removed at the end of Duration.
SpeechToText
Setup
  • CommunityToolkit.Maui.Core references System.Speech 10.0.11 on Windows (see All packages).
Smaller changes
  • StartListenAsync with null options throws ArgumentNullException from the call (see All packages: null arguments). With valid options, a canceled token still returns a canceled Task, so awaiting it throws OperationCanceledException.
  • On Windows, and for a start from a background thread on iOS and Mac Catalyst, an interrupted StartListenAsync completes without an exception and without listening, even if its token is canceled afterwards.
    • Here "interrupted" means StopListenAsync or DisposeAsync (on Windows, also a newer StartListenAsync) is called while the start waits for the platform.
StateContainer
Behavior
  • StateContainer. A StateKey that is not defined throws StateContainerException with its own message and no inner exception. It used to throw the "assigned to multiple StateViews" message, so change any code that matches the message text.
StatusBar and StatusBarBehavior
API
  • StatusBarBehavior requires Android 6.0 (API 23). The Android type is now [SupportedOSPlatform("android23.0")], like StatusBar already was.
    • C# code that uses it in a project with a lower minimum Android version (the .NET MAUI templates use 21) gets warning CA1416, which fails builds that treat warnings as errors.
    • What to do: raise the minimum Android version to 23, or create the behavior inside if (OperatingSystem.IsIOS() || OperatingSystem.IsAndroidVersionAtLeast(23)). Not IsAndroidVersionAtLeast(23) alone: it is false on iOS.
    • A StatusBarBehavior declared in XAML gets no warning.
    • Nothing changes at run time: on Android 5.0 and 5.1 it did nothing before and still does nothing.
    • CommunityToolkit.Maui's minimum Android version stays 5.0 (API 21), the same as .NET MAUI 10's.
Setup
  • iOS: remove UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance from Info.plist if you set it to false for StatusBar.SetStyle (see Behavior below).
  • Android: StatusBarBehavior needs a minimum Android version of 23 or a guard (see API above). CommunityToolkit.Maui's minimum Android version stays 5.0 (API 21), the same as .NET MAUI 10's.
Behavior
  • iOS, .NET 10: StatusBar.SetStyle and StatusBarBehavior. SetStyle no longer needs UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance set to false in Info.plist.
    • The first LightContent or DarkContent replaces preferredStatusBarStyle until the app ends, for every view controller that does not choose its own style (the system pickers included). Default gives each view controller its own style back.
    • With the key set to false, the style still applies in apps built with an iOS SDK before 27, but not with the iOS 27 SDK (Xcode 27): the app keeps its status bar style and the call writes a trace message. So remove the key from Info.plist.
    • SetStyle called off the main thread throws UIKitThreadAccessException, in Release builds too, so call it on the main thread.
Smaller changes
  • On Android 15+, colors without alpha no longer paint the bars black. On iOS, the status bar color view follows rotation and lets touches through, and on iOS 26 it comes back after an iPhone turns back to portrait.
StringToListConverter
Smaller changes
  • StringToListConverter splits at the entry of a one-entry Separators list, as documented; before, it split at Separator.
TouchBehavior
Smaller changes
  • Windows selects the tapped CollectionView item. On Android and Windows, a tap on a header, footer or empty view selects nothing.
  • The state events are raised at once with the new value.
  • ShouldMakeChildrenInputTransparent takes effect when it changes.
  • A NaN DefaultOpacity, HoveredOpacity or PressedOpacity throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, where 15.0.1 accepted it.
  • On Windows, a release now ends every press, as on Android (iOS also cancels a touch for good once it has left the element). Whatever CurrentHoverStatus says, a release over the element completes the tap (Command, TouchGestureCompleted), and a release outside it cancels.
    • Before, a Windows release completed only while the hover status was Entered. So a release outside the element could complete, and one over it could leave the press running.
UserStoppedTypingBehavior
API
  • Null arguments: The async void overrides of UserStoppedTypingBehavior throw to the caller instead of posting the exception to the SynchronizationContext.
Behavior
  • Keyboard dismissal. UserStoppedTypingBehavior hides the keyboard only while its own InputView has the focus, and through the view's own window. So Android no longer hides the keyboard of the view the user moved to, and the keyboard goes away in a modal page or a Popup too. No action is needed.
  • UserStoppedTypingBehavior.StoppedTypingTimeThreshold rejects a negative value. A negative value is ignored and the previous value is kept (MAUI logs a warning). Before, it failed inside Task.Delay. Use 0 or more.
Validation behaviors
API
  • Null arguments: The async void overrides of ValidationBehavior throw to the caller instead of posting the exception to the SynchronizationContext.
Smaller changes
  • Validation behaviors validate again when a rule changes. Errors is set on the UI thread, and IsRunning is reset after a cancel.

What's Changed

entry.title: dotnet/SqlClient - Releases - 2026-11-09
entry.content:
Preview Release v8.0.0-preview1

This first 8.0 preview includes changes since the release/7.1 branch point, 92f220956b07328054701a869f452cade51830c1 (2026-09-15), through b87ca6e7643611ddc3273324de346d09e8ff2c43. Changes already shipped in 7.1.1 are identified below because the branch-cut baseline predates that release.

The driver and its four companion packages use package version 8.0.0-preview1. The family AssemblyVersion changes from 7.0.0.0 to 8.0.0.0; .NET Framework applications should review strong-name binding redirects when upgrading. Native SNI and Microsoft.SqlServer.Server remain independently versioned.

Companion package release notes

  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.AlwaysEncrypted.AzureKeyVaultProvider 8.0.0-preview1
  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Extensions.Azure 8.0.0-preview1
  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Extensions.Abstractions 8.0.0-preview1
  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Internal.Logging 8.0.0-preview1

Added

Vector float16 support and per-connection version negotiation

What Changed:

  • Added support for SQL Server vector(N, float16), including reader values, parameters, output parameters, column schema, and bulk copy. On modern .NET, use SqlVector<Half>; the existing SqlVector<float> API remains supported. (#4501)
  • Added the Vector Type Support connection-string keyword and SqlConnectionStringBuilder.VectorTypeSupport, of type SqlVectorTypeSupport. Values are Off, V1, and V2; the default is V2.

Who Benefits:

  • Applications storing embeddings can use float16 vectors with smaller element payloads, while choosing the result-type contract independently for each connection.

Impact:

  • Result-type change: when the server negotiates V2, modern .NET returns native SqlVector<Half> values for float16 columns instead of JSON strings. Set Vector Type Support=v1 to preserve float16 JSON-string results, or off to receive all vector columns as text. Different settings use separate connection pools.
  • .NET Framework has no System.Half. Float16 columns remain available as JSON strings or through GetSqlVector<float>, which widens their elements exactly. Prefer the latter when reading many values, to avoid the additional JSON serialization.
  • GetColumnSchema() exposes VectorBaseType and VectorDimensions through the column indexer when native vector metadata is negotiated.
  • SQL Server performs cross-base conversion for native vector parameters and bulk-copy inputs. Typed vectors are not automatically serialized for text destinations; supply JSON strings or an explicit SQL cast instead. Vector TVPs are not added by this change.
  • Float16 requires a server that supports it; enable PREVIEW_FEATURES while the server feature is in preview. See the float16 sample.
var builder = new SqlConnectionStringBuilder(connectionString)
{
    VectorTypeSupport = SqlVectorTypeSupport.V1
};

Opt-in reset of pooled transaction isolation levels

What Changed:

  • Added Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EnableTransactionIsolationLevelReset, default false. When enabled, a SqlClient-tracked isolation-level change is reset to READ COMMITTED before pooled reuse when no existing enlistment or active delegated transaction root remains. (#96, #4330)

Who Benefits:

  • Applications that otherwise inherit an isolation level left by a previous user of a pooled connection.

Impact:

  • Enable the switch before opening connections. A necessary reset adds a round trip and uses the remaining open-timeout budget. Known Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool endpoints are excluded; the default preserves existing behavior.
  • A user-issued SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL alone does not mark the connection for this reset. The switch is not general cleanup for arbitrary T-SQL session changes.

Additional TimeOnly write paths (net10.0 only)

What Changed:

  • Added TimeOnly support for SqlBulkCopy DataRow/DataTable sources and SqlParameter values with SqlDbType.Variant, writing SQL time values. (#4604)

Who Benefits:

  • Applications using modern .NET time-only values in bulk-copy and variant workflows.

Impact:

  • These paths no longer require conversion to TimeSpan. This does not add TimeOnly to .NET Framework.

Authentication diagnostics

What Changed:

  • The Azure extension forwards MSAL, allowlisted Azure.Identity, and SqlClient token acquisition events to Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EventSource using the new AuthenticationTrace keyword (0x2000). (#1846, #4872)

Who Benefits:

  • Support teams can diagnose built-in Entra ID authentication without implementing a custom provider or logging callback.

Impact:

  • Collect authentication events with 0x2000, or authentication plus ordinary trace with 0x2002. On modern .NET:

    dotnet-trace collect --process-id <pid> --providers Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EventSource:0x2000:5 --rundown false

  • On .NET Framework, use ETW or an in-process EventListener. PII logging remains disabled for extension-owned requests. Correlation is best effort; some Azure.Identity events have an empty connection ID and can originate from application-owned credentials. Treat captures as sensitive operational data.

  • See the Azure extension notes for limitations and the logging sample.

Changed

Breaking change: minimum modern runtime is .NET 10

What Changed:

  • Replaced the net8.0 and net9.0 driver implementation targets with net10.0. .NET Framework 4.6.2 support is retained. (#4779)

Who Benefits:

  • Applications moving to the .NET 10 runtime and dependency servicing band.

Impact:

  • Upgrade modern applications to .NET 10, or remain on a compatible earlier driver. Retained netstandard2.0 reference/unsupported-platform assets do not extend driver runtime support to .NET 8 or .NET 9.

Breaking change: TCP MultiSubnetFailover is enabled by default

What Changed:

  • When omitted from the connection string, MultiSubnetFailover now defaults to true for TCP connections. TransparentNetworkIPResolution defaults to false on .NET Framework. (#4876, #4927)

Who Benefits:

  • Applications connecting to multi-address hosts try resolved IP addresses in parallel, without needing an explicit opt-in.

Impact:

  • Explicit values remain authoritative. The automatic default is disabled for non-TCP protocols, LocalDB, database mirroring partners, admin:/via:, and unprefixed local servers using native SNI. Explicit true still fails with unsupported protocols or failover partners. MSF retains its 64-address limit.
  • With native SNI on Windows, an unprefixed remote host now uses TCP only, without Named Pipes fallback. Use np: or MultiSubnetFailover=false when needed.
  • With MSF enabled, IPAddressPreference and TNIR are ignored. The builder reports the keyword default, not the routing decision for a particular connection.
  • Restore the old MSF default with Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EnableMultiSubnetFailoverByDefault=false. On .NET Framework, also set Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.DisableTNIRByDefaultInConnectionString=false to restore the previous TNIR default. Set switches before using SqlClient. See networking migration guidance.

Breaking change: Azure Attestation requires the Azure extension

What Changed:

  • Moved Azure Attestation token validation and the IdentityModel dependencies from the core driver to Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Extensions.Azure. (#4017, #4790)

Who Benefits:

  • Applications not using Azure Attestation no longer receive these dependencies from core.

Impact:

  • Applications using Attestation Protocol=AAS must explicitly reference the matching Azure extension. Without it, enclave session setup throws InvalidOperationException.
  • The Azure extension now depends on Azure.Core rather than Azure.Identity. Credential namespaces are unchanged. Remove direct Azure.Identity references older than 1.21.0, or upgrade to 1.21.0 or later; Azure.Identity.Broker users need 1.6.0 or later. (#4749)

Breaking changes: reference API and argument validation corrections

What Changed:

  • Reference APIs now match implementation accessibility and sealing, and no longer expose the nonexistent SqlBatchCommand.CanCreateParameter setter on .NET Framework. (#4832, #4890)
  • SqlParameterCollection.RemoveAt(int) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, rather than IndexOutOfRangeException, for an invalid index; indexer behavior is unchanged. (#4874)
  • Character-type SqlMetaData construction in globalization-invariant mode requires an overload with an explicit LCID (net10.0 only). (#4457)

Who Benefits:

  • Consumers get accurate compile-time API contracts and explicit argument validation.

Impact:

  • Correct code that instantiated inaccessible types, derived from sealed data-classification types, or assigned the nonexistent setter. Update exception handling for RemoveAt(int).
  • Use a constructor with locale or localeId for character metadata in invariant mode; this does not add general globalization-invariant connection support.

Package layout and family-version validation

  • Managed driver implementations now reside in lib/net462 and lib/net10.0, without duplicated RID-specific managed DLLs. Update custom scripts copying from runtimes/<rid>/lib/<tfm>/Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.dll. Native SNI remains separate. (#4673)
  • Consumer builds emit warning SQLCLIENT001 for mismatched installed family package versions, including preview suffixes. Use matching driver and companion versions. Native SNI and Microsoft.SqlServer.Server are excluded; setting SqlClientEnforceFamilyVersions=false disables the check. (#4815)
  • Corrected Source Link mappings and package source coverage. This branch-cut delta was also backported to 7.1; it is not unique to 8.0. (#4710)

Windows connection pool identity isolation (Windows only)

  • Pool identity includes the Windows logon session, separating network-only impersonation sessions even when their local SID is identical. Reusing tokens from the same logon session preserves reuse; distinct sessions can increase pool counts. (#4814)
  • See connection pooling and impersonation.

Trimming and authentication configuration

  • Authentication registration/bootstrap now lives in Abstractions, allowing SqlAuthenticationProvider.GetProvider/SetProvider to use the shared registry without loading the driver through reflection. SqlAuthenticationInitializer also lives in Abstractions, with a type forward preserving existing references. Abstractions adds a trim/AOT-analyzed net10.0 asset. (#4821)

  • Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EnableAppConfig controls authentication configuration on both .NET Framework and modern .NET. The driver's separate retry-configuration and switch-override readers use this switch on modern .NET only; they remain unchanged on .NET Framework. (#4697, #4821)

  • Added Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EnableAzureExtensionDiscovery for reflective authentication-provider discovery. Both authentication switches default to true and cache their first value. Explicit provider registration remains available when discovery is disabled. Authentication discovery does not control the driver's separate Azure Attestation loader.

  • For explicit registration in trimmed/Native AOT applications, disable both reflective paths at publish time, then explicitly construct/register a provider for every required method before opening connections. Runtime switch values alone cannot remove code during publication.

    <ItemGroup>
  <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EnableAppConfig"
                                  Value="false" Trim="true" />
  <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EnableAzureExtensionDiscovery"
                                  Value="false" Trim="true" />
</ItemGroup>

  • Trimmed JIT applications can retain enabled reflective paths if they preserve the configuration infrastructure, handlers, provider/initializer constructors, and Azure discovery contracts. Enabling a switch does not root these members. Enabled paths report trimming warnings and, for Native AOT, dynamic-code warnings.

  • Source-generated JSON serialization replaces reflection-based calls for vector conversions and enclave attestation, including the asynchronous HGS request path, reducing trimming and dynamic-code warnings (net10.0 only). JSON representations remain unchanged. (#4683, #4801)

  • Reduced trimming/AOT warnings in diagnostics, schema metadata, server discovery, and native interop (net10.0 only). These are incremental improvements, not complete Native AOT support. (#4684, #4688, #4703)

  • Authentication section handlers are public in Abstractions; existing driver-qualified app.config declarations remain supported. Configured providers/initializers take precedence over application registrations, which take precedence over Azure defaults. Failed explicit configuration does not silently select an earlier/default provider; failures are traced, and explicit successful application registration can recover a failed method. Check SetProvider's return value and trace diagnostics when registering. (#4816, #4860, #4821)

Performance and sync/async pathways

  • Reduced allocations in Always Encrypted key handling and cache contention for parallel encryption-key lookups. Calls to key-store providers to decrypt column encryption keys remain serialized. (#4256)
  • Converted asynchronous SqlBulkCopy setup, including metadata retrieval and connection recovery, to native async/await. The per-row asynchronous copy loop is unchanged. (#4687)
  • Added asynchronous enclave-provider and delegate operations, including awaited attestation HTTP requests and retry delays. This is groundwork, not end-to-end nonblocking Always Encrypted command execution: the new operations are not yet wired into the command execution path, and driver key-store resolution remains synchronous for both sync and async commands. (#4541, #4886)

Other changes

  • The user-agent Driver Properties mask now reports configured UseCompatibilityAsyncBehaviour and UseCompatibilityProcessSni values through bits 0x2 and 0x4, respectively. These report configuration before compatibility overrides, not effective behavior; async defaults are unchanged. (#4911)
  • Added diagnostics for database-context mismatches after transparent reconnection, without changing recovery behavior. (#4130)
  • Documentation now explains complete reader consumption for InfoMessage delivery and trailing errors. Read()/ReadAsync() ending a result does not establish batch success: with default behavior, advance through NextResult()/NextResultAsync() until false, including after empty results. Cleanup still suppresses pending nonfatal errors; SingleRow and SingleResult retain their discard semantics. Reader runtime behavior is unchanged. (#4723, #4729)
  • Clarified Prepare incompatibility with optimized parameter binding and SqlBatch command-behavior exceptions. (#4726, #4878)
  • Updated shipping dependencies, including the cryptography servicing fixes. Concrete direct dependency floors are listed below and in the companion notes. (#4848, #4880)
  • Updated Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SNI and Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SNI.runtime from 7.1.0 to 8.0.0-preview1.26309.4 (Windows native SNI only). (#5011)

Fixed

  • Malformed PRELOGIN option headers, offsets, lengths, and response sizes now produce a parsing error (InvalidOperationException) during Open/OpenAsync, rather than incidental IndexOutOfRangeException failures. (#4902)
  • Responses missing required row metadata or authentication state now produce a corrupted-stream parsing error and invalidate the connection, rather than causing null-reference failures or falling back to unrelated result metadata. The parsing error is an InvalidOperationException, not a SqlException. (#4941)
  • Managed SNI honors an explicit HostNameInCertificate as the sole expected certificate hostname, rather than accepting a match only to the destination (net10.0, managed SNI only). Certificate-chain and ServerCertificate checks are unchanged. (#4905)
  • Fixed managed-SNI parallel TCP connection attempts failing when one address errors immediately despite another reachable address; unused sockets are disposed (net10.0, managed SNI only). (#4929)
  • Fixed the managed-SNI MARS receive teardown race that could leave an unobserved callback exception during disposal (net10.0, managed SNI only). (#4680)
  • Fixed HasRows returning false when multiple informational messages precede rows. (#4773)
  • Fixed XML streaming failures for fragments beginning with text by explicitly selecting UTF-16LE when creating the XML reader. (#4757)
  • Fixed corrupted nvarchar text from GetTextReader() with SequentialAccess on big-endian platforms; little-endian behavior is unchanged (big-endian only). (#4945)
  • Fixed SqlBulkCopy losing money/smallmoney type identity in sql_variant values. (#4727)
  • Fixed configurable retry logic retrying a command outside its original transaction after the error aborted that transaction. (#4728)
  • Reassert non-ReadCommitted isolation levels when pooled connections reattach to the same ambient transaction with a pending reset. This unconditional correctness fix can add a round trip and is separate from the opt-in reset switch. (#4335)
  • Prevent V1/V2 pool pruning from retiring pools with in-flight acquisition, physical creation, or background replenishment, preserving transaction-affine reuse and avoiding unintended transaction promotion. Explicit clear/shutdown semantics are unchanged. (#4755, #4754)
  • Isolate cached enclave sessions by attestation protocol, server, database, and URL. (#4829)
  • Retry providers load/resolve in SqlClient's current AssemblyLoadContext, rather than the default context (net10.0 only). Collectible contexts using managed SNI can unload; this does not promise native-SNI unloadability. (#4588)
  • Prevent eager native SNI initialization on non-Windows platforms (net10.0 on Linux/macOS). (#4700)
  • Fixed the nullable statistics execution-timer race and active soft-connection counter drift when the default wait-handle pool reclaims abandoned connections. Concurrent use of a connection is still unsupported. (#4875, #4725)
  • Formatter-based SqlException serialization preserves Errors and derived error properties such as Number, addressing .NET Framework remoting scenarios. Formatter serialization remains obsolete on modern .NET; this is not guidance to use BinaryFormatter or deserialize untrusted data. (#1940, #4622)
  • Restored SqlParameterCollection.Add(string, object) and exposed Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Server.TriggerAction in the reference assembly (net462 only). The former remains obsolete; prefer AddWithValue or explicitly typed parameters. (#4832)
  • Windows WAM missing-parent-window errors now explain alternatives for windowless hosts, preserving the MSAL error code and inner exception (Windows only, Azure extension). (#4858)

Included in the branch-cut delta, already shipped in 7.1.1

  • Fixed zero-valued decimal parameters with equal precision and scale. (#4721)
  • Fixed expired/nearly expired access-token eviction in opt-in connection pool V2. (#4734)
  • Preserve admitted in-flight opens during pool clearing, discarding connections returned to the retired pool. (#4718)

These are retained because the requested baseline predates 7.1.1; they are not new fixes for applications already using that release.

Removed

Breaking change: SQL Server 2005 compatibility

What Changed:

  • Removed SQL Server 2005 connectivity and Type System Version=SQL Server 2005, including its date/time-as-string and large-UDT-as-binary compatibility projections. (#4881)

Impact:

  • SQL Server 2005 connections are rejected. Remove that type-system setting and update code that depended on its projections to consume current date/time and UDT representations.

Contributors

We thank the following public contributors for their contributions to this release:

  • alaricd
  • charlesroddie
  • edwardneal
  • sharpjs
  • shreyarao4
  • virzak

Target Platform Support

  • .NET Framework 4.6.2+ on Windows.
  • .NET 10.0+ on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
  • netstandard2.0 assets are for reference/unsupported-platform scenarios only.

entry.content:
core-1.21.0-rc.2

The following changes are from the previous release 1.21.0-rc.1.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry v1.21.0-rc.2

    • Fixed an exception when downscaling empty exponential histogram buckets after
      a reset.
      (#8064)

    • Fixed tracing callbacks continuing after provider shutdown or disposal on older
      target frameworks.
      (#8065)

    • Fixed initialization failures when environment variable access is denied.
      Configuration reloads retain the last successful values when access is denied.
      (#8070)

    • Fixed a source, meter or legacy activity name with a trailing line feed
      matching a wildcard pattern which does not end in a wildcard.
      (#8074)

    • Fixed OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES values being decoded as form data, which
      changed a + to a space. Values are now only percent-decoded, as defined by
      the Resource SDK specification.
      (#8074)

    • Updated the schema URL of resources created by the SDK to use OpenTelemetry
      Semantic Conventions version 1.45.0.
      (#8079)

    • Added support for batching the metric points exported by
      PeriodicExportingMetricReader. When a maximum export batch size is set,
      using the new constructor overload or
      PeriodicExportingMetricReaderOptions.MaxExportBatchSize, the metric
      points of each collection are split into batches of at most that many
      metric points, even if that splits up the metric points of a single
      metric. The batches are exported serially with the export timeout
      applying to each export. It can also be configured with the
      OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_MAX_BATCH_SIZE environment variable.
      (#8053)

    • Fixed PeriodicExportingMetricReader exporting a collection which was still
      in progress when Shutdown() timed out to its exporter after the exporter
      had been shut down.
      (#8053)

    • Fixed PeriodicExportingMetricReader not making its final collection when
      Shutdown() was called before its background task had started running on
      platforms where threading is not available, such as browsers.
      (#8053)

    • OTEL_DIAGNOSTICS.json now uses the SelfDiagnosticsOptions pipeline,
      adding configuration warnings and a redacted environment snapshot to each
      file's preamble. Verbose and LogAlways also log loaded assemblies.
      File-open failures are reported on standard error.
      (#7997)

    • Breaking Change OTEL_DIAGNOSTICS.json now writes rolling
      otel-dotnet-*.log files in the standard entry format instead of a circular
      {executable}.{pid}.log file. FileSize is split evenly across two
      retained files, so total disk usage stays close to the configured limit.
      FormatMessage is now ignored; messages are always formatted.
      Provider-configured sinks, including those enabled through environment
      variables, override the JSON configuration with a warning event. Writes are
      asynchronous and may drop entries when the bounded queue fills.
      (#7997)

    • Added Sampler.Shutdown and the overridable Sampler.OnShutdown to allow
      samplers to release resources, as described in the
      specification.
      TracerProvider now calls Shutdown on its sampler when it is shut down or
      disposed, and ParentBasedSampler and AlwaysRecordSampler call Shutdown
      on the samplers they delegate to.
      (#8060)

    • The TracerProvider now disposes of its sampler after its listener has
      stopped calling the sampler, rather than before the processors are shut down.
      (#8060)

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Api v1.21.0-rc.2

    • Improve traceparent extraction throughput on .NET.
      (#8095)

    • Changed EnvironmentVariableCarrier snapshots to preserve environment variable
      names, preventing extraction from non-normalized aliases and collisions with
      normalized names. Process environment snapshots now follow the platform's
      case-sensitivity rules.
      (#8098)

    • The experimental APIs previously covered by OTEL1005
      (EnvironmentVariableCarrier) are now stable.
      (#8044)

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Api.ProviderBuilderExtensions v1.21.0-rc.2

    No notable changes.

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Console v1.21.0-rc.2

    • An OutOfMemoryException thrown while converting an attribute value to a
      string is no longer swallowed and the attribute dropped; it now propagates.
      (#7929)

    • Added support for batching the metric points exported by the periodic
      exporting metric reader. Set
      PeriodicExportingMetricReaderOptions.MaxExportBatchSize to limit the
      number of metric points in each exported batch. It can also be configured
      with the OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_MAX_BATCH_SIZE environment variable.
      (#8053)

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Exporter.InMemory v1.21.0-rc.2

    • Added support for batching the metric points exported by the periodic
      exporting metric reader. Set
      PeriodicExportingMetricReaderOptions.MaxExportBatchSize to limit the
      number of metric points in each exported batch. It can also be configured
      with the OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_MAX_BATCH_SIZE environment variable.
      (#8053)

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol v1.21.0-rc.2

    • Fixed unbounded resource serialization buffer growth and incorrect buffer
      reuse after buffer allocation failures.
      (#8069)

    • Fixed exporter option initialization failing when environment variable access
      is denied.
      (#8070)

    • Fixed OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (and the Headers option) being decoded
      before it was split into headers, so that a percent-encoded , in a value
      started a new header and encoded leading or trailing whitespace was removed.
      (#8075)

    • Fixed the retry delay of a gRPC response being ignored or misread when a
      length which does not fit in an int was truncated instead of being
      rejected.
      (#8075)

    • Fixed the retry delay of a gRPC response being ignored or misread when a
      field did not have the wire type that its number defines, instead of the
      field being skipped.
      (#8075)

    • Fixed the retry delay of a gRPC response being misread when the retry_delay
      field was repeated, instead of the occurrences being merged.
      (#8075)

    • Fixed the retry delay of a gRPC response being ignored when the
      grpc-status-details-bin trailer was Base64-encoded without padding, as
      emitted by gRPC-Go.
      (#8075)

    • The retry delay in the grpc-status-details-bin trailer of a gRPC response is
      now ignored if the status code in the details contradicts the grpc-status
      of the response.
      (#8078)

    • Attribute values implementing IUtf8SpanFormattable (.NET 10+) that are not
      already handled as a built-in type are now formatted directly into the export
      buffer with TryFormat and exported as string attributes, instead of through
      ToString().
      (#7929)

    • An OutOfMemoryException thrown while converting an attribute value to a
      string is no longer swallowed and the attribute dropped; it now propagates.
      (#7929)

    • Fixed string attribute values truncated by an attribute value length limit
      ending in half of a surrogate pair. The truncated value now ends before the
      pair instead.
      (#7929)

    • Added support for batching the metric points exported by the periodic
      exporting metric reader. Set
      PeriodicExportingMetricReaderOptions.MaxExportBatchSize to limit the
      number of metric points in each exported batch. It can also be configured
      with the OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_MAX_BATCH_SIZE environment variable.
      (#8053)

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Zipkin v1.21.0-rc.2

    • Fixed exporter option initialization failing when environment variable access
      is denied.
      (#8070)

    • An OutOfMemoryException thrown while converting an attribute value to a
      string is no longer swallowed and the attribute dropped; it now propagates.
      (#7929)

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting v1.21.0-rc.2

    • Fixed host resource detection throwing SecurityException when configuration
      values cannot be read.
      (#8070)

    • Updated the schema URL of resources created by the host environment resource
      detector to use OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions version 1.45.0.
      (#8079)

    See CHANGELOG for details.

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Propagators v1.21.0-rc.2

    No notable changes.

    See CHANGELOG for details.

Instrumentation.Kusto-0.1.0-alpha.8

  • NuGet: OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Kusto v0.1.0-alpha.8

    • Updated Semantic Conventions version to 1.45.0.
      (#5833)

    • Breaking change: The server.port attribute is no longer recorded when the
      port is the default port for the scheme of the cluster URI (for example 443
      for https), to follow the v1.45.0 database semantic conventions.
      (#5833)

    • Fixed query text sanitization taking quadratic time for queries with many
      signed numeric literals when RecordQueryText is enabled.
      (#5937)

    • Fixed excessive CPU usage when generating db.query.summary for queries
      containing a very large number of materialized_view() calls.
      (#5938)

    • Fixed literal values not being sanitized in db.query.text for control
      commands the Kusto grammar does not recognize (such as .list blobs).
      (#5936)

    • Fixed failed operations exporting the error message returned by the cluster as
      the span status description. The message is now only recorded as an exception
      event when the new RecordException option is enabled.
      (#5911)

    • Fixed a client request id or database name containing text= being able to
      bypass db.query.text sanitization and set db.query.summary.
      (#5913)

    • Fixed db.query.summary generation consuming excessive CPU and memory for
      some queries. Table names are now identified from the query syntax, so
      db.query.summary may differ for some queries (for example, column names
      are no longer included).
      (#5912)

    See CHANGELOG for details.
